items.name: Chlorine
items.note: A sharp green gas that cleans water and makes salt with sodium.

items.name: Hydrogen
items.note: The lightest element and the most common in the universe; with oxygen it makes water.

items.name: Nickel
items.note: A metal used in coins, batteries, and stainless steel.

items.name: Silver
items.note: The best carrier of electricity of any metal; used in mirrors, coins, and circuits.

items.name: Zinc
items.note: Used to coat steel against rust and to help the body heal.

items.name: Copper
items.note: The metal of wires and pipes; it has carried electricity since the first telegraph.

items.name: Potassium
items.note: A metal the body needs for nerves and muscles; it feeds plants as potash.

items.name: Calcium
items.note: The metal of bones, teeth, milk, and chalk.

items.name: Sulfur
items.note: The yellow element of matches, gunpowder, and volcanic fumes.

items.name: Tin
items.note: The metal of tin cans, solder, and bronze.

items.name: Oxygen
items.note: About 21 parts in 100 of the air; fires burn and lungs breathe because of it.

items.name: Helium
items.note: A noble gas that reacts with almost nothing; it lifts balloons and cools scanner magnets.

items.name: Gold
items.note: The metal of coins, jewellery, and phone contacts; it never corrodes.

items.name: Carbon
items.note: The backbone of living things; diamond, graphite, coal, and oil are all carbon.

items.name: Nitrogen
items.note: About 78 parts in 100 of the air; it keeps food fresh in sealed bags.

items.name: Silicon
items.note: The heart of computer chips and solar cells; sand and glass are mostly silicon.

items.name: Sodium
items.note: A soft metal that joins with chlorine to make common salt.

items.name: Aluminium
items.note: A light, strong metal used in aircraft, cans, and window frames.

items.name: Lead
items.note: A heavy, soft metal used in batteries, shields, and weights.

items.name: Iron
items.note: The most used metal in the world: bridges, tools, and the red cells of blood.
